Subject: Request: quarterly invoicing + conditional SLA credit for pilot

Hi Mina,

Thanks again for the product demo last week — the engineering team is excited to pilot Redwood for inference-heavy features. Our procurement lead asked whether you can support a quarterly invoicing cadence for the pilot and allow Net-90 payment terms.

Quick context: LyraHealth’s fiscal calendar and centralized accounts-payable team only runs disbursements each quarter for pilot spend under $250k. If we can invoice quarterly (aggregate usage for the quarter and issue one invoice) and accept Net-90, we can proceed without raising an out-of-cycle PO.

Two asks from procurement:
- Quarterly invoicing for the pilot (Nov–Jan quarter to be billed together)
- Net-90 payment terms on the aggregated invoice
- A small SLA credit if uptime drops below the promised 99.5% during the pilot (procurement would like a 3% credit applied to the affected quarter)

We can commit to a 3-month pilot and a minimum usage floor (~$45k) for that period. If quarterly invoicing is possible, we’ll provide a PO and sign the attached MAA. Also happy to get onto a quick call to walk through the mechanics.

Best,
Claire
Claire Huang
Head of Partnerships, LyraHealth
procure@lyrahealth.com

Attachment: MAA_Draft_v1.pdf (referenced)

Hi Claire — thanks for the clear ask and the pilot commitment. This is a common procurement rhythm for some of our larger health customers, and we should be able to support quarterly invoicing with a few guardrails from the Deal Desk and Finance.

Looping in Jonas (Deal Desk) and Vanessa (VP, Sales) to confirm the commercial tradeoffs. Proposed next steps from our side:
1) Deal Desk to confirm whether Net-90 + quarterly invoice can be allowed for a 3-month pilot and what controls Finance needs.
2) If approved, we’ll issue a single invoice at quarter close with line-item usage detail and a specified SLA-credit mechanism.
3) Legal to redline the attached MAA and SOW Appendix. We’ll send a DocuSign when final.

A couple of points for clarity:
- Do you expect the SLA credit to be automatic based on our monitoring or applied after an incident/post-mortem?
- If payment lapses and extends beyond Net-90, Finance will require interest and an auto-conversion to monthly billing at renewal.

Jonas/Vanessa — can you weigh in on the approval path and any additional commercial requirements (min. commitment, prepayment, PO sighting)?

Thanks — Mina
Mina Haddad
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachments: MAA_Draft_v1.pdf, SOW_AppendixA.docx

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Request: quarterly invoicing + conditional SLA credit for pilot

Mina / Claire — I reviewed the ask with Finance. We can provisionally approve quarterly invoicing + Net-90 for the 3-month pilot under these conditions:

- Term: Pilot = first 3 months (one quarter). Redwood will issue a single invoice at the end of the quarter that aggregates usage and applies any SLA credits.
- SLA credit: Up to 5% credit for the quarter if uptime < 99.5%. Credits are applied at quarter close after our incident review; they are not auto-processed until the post-incident reconciliation is complete.
- Minimum commitment: $45,000 total for the pilot (invoice will reflect usage; if usage < floor we will invoice the floor amount).
- Payment terms: Net-90 from invoice date. If payment is not received by day 95, Finance will add a 1.5% monthly interest on outstanding balance and require a conversion to monthly billing for any subsequent renewal term.
- Security/legal: Signed MAA + executed Security Addendum required before data plane onboarding.
- PO: Procurement PO ok to be provided post-signature but must reference deal id DL-78321 on the invoice.

If LyraHealth agrees to those bullets, we’ll create a revised MAA (attached) and route DocuSign. Also adding a small operational note: to create the quarterly invoice we’ll need usage exports at the end of each month to reconcile prior to billing close.

I’ve attached a short deal_terms_summary.csv with the approved guardrails for internal Finance/RevOps.

— Jonas
Jonas Weber

Attachments: deal_terms_summary.csv
